extracted.intended_audience: General readers, researchers, students, and policymakers interested in US video game legislation and policy
extracted.subtask_description: Summary and provisions of the 2005 proposed U.S. federal bill (Family Entertainment Protection Act) that would mandate enforcement of ESRB ratings and authorize FTC actions, penalties, audits, and reporting to protect minors from inappropriate video game content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal mandate enforcement of the ESRB ratings system
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill called for a federal mandate enforcement of the Entertainment Software Rating Board (ESRB) ratings system for video games in order to protect children from inappropriate content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching intent of the bill: to rely on ESRB ratings but compel federal enforcement mechanisms to ensure minors cannot access Mature or Adults-Only games. The bill couples reliance on industry ratings with government oversight measures described in subsequent provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on selling Mature and Adults Only video games to minors (penalties)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prohibition against any business from selling or renting a Mature, Adults-Only, or Ratings Pending game to a person who is younger than seventeen, with fines/community service for violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified penalties: on-site store managers would be subject to a fine of $1,000 or 100 hours of community service for the first offense; $5,000 or 500 hours of community service for each subsequent offense. The provision is not aimed at punishing retailers who act in good faith; retailers would have an affirmative defense if they were shown an identification they believed to be valid or have a system in place to display and enforce the ESRB system. Similar state laws (California, Michigan, Illinois) had been enacted but later overturned as unconstitutional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative defense for retailers enforcing ESRB
rubrics_metrics.description: Retailers would have an affirmative defense if they were shown an identification they believed to be valid or have a system in place to display and enforce the ESRB system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits the bill's punitive reach by protecting retailers who reasonably attempted to verify age or who maintained compliance procedures; it is explicitly stated to avoid punishing good-faith enforcement efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual, independent analysis of the ratings system
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill requires an annual, independent analysis of game ratings to ensure the ESRB ratings system accurately reflects game content and does not change significantly over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: oversight of the industry's self-regulatory rating process. The analysis is intended to verify accuracy and stability of ratings year-to-year, since the bill relies on the industry to continue rating appropriateness for minors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for the FTC to investigate misleading or inaccurate ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill requires the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to conduct an investigation to determine whether incidents of inconsistent or misleading ratings (e.g., the 'Hot Coffee' GTA: San Andreas issue) are pervasive, and includes a Sense of Congress that the Commission shall take appropriate action if it determines there is a pervasive problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provision empowers the FTC to look into whether ESRB ratings have failed to disclose or properly classify content. It contemplates remedial action by the FTC if systemic issues are found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to register consumer complaints and FTC Bureau of Consumer Protection reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill requires the Bureau of Consumer Protection (BCP) of the FTC to ensure consumers can file complaints if they find content to be misleading or deceptive and requires the BCP to report on the number of such complaints to Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates a consumer-facing mechanism for reporting misleading ratings/content and mandates transparency to Congress via complaint counts, enabling oversight and measurement of consumer concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual retailer audit (secret shopper survey) authorized for FTC
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill authorizes the FTC to conduct an annual, random audit of retailers—sometimes referred to as a secret shopper survey—to determine how easy it is for young people to purchase Mature and Adults Only video games and report the findings to Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This operationalizes enforcement by measuring retailer compliance in practice through random checks and reporting results to Congress, providing empirical evidence of enforcement effectiveness or gaps.
